321501.title: Regularity conjecture for uniquely $K_r$-saturated graphs
321501.literal_statement:
Let $r$ be a positive integer. A graph is **uniquely $K_r$-saturated** if it is $K_r$-free and adding any missing edge creates exactly one copy of $K_r$; a **dominating vertex** is a vertex adjacent to every other vertex. A graph is **regular** if all its vertices have the same degree.

**Regularity conjecture.** For each $r$, a uniquely $K_r$-saturated graph with no dominating vertex is regular.

All examples known in the source are regular, which motivates this conjecture. Its resolution is not supplied and remains open in the paper's context.
321501.actual_review_depth: Stolee original regularity motivation; Hartke–Stolee Construction 23 and Figure 19, PDF pages 34 and 37. Figure visually read.
321501.ordinary_attempt_and_prior_scope: The published 16-vertex 5-primitive graph has degrees 8 at v1,v2 and 9 at the fourteen other vertices, hence no degree-15 dominating vertex and is irregular. Its printed uniquely K5-saturated property directly refutes the universal regularity claim.
321501.precise_remaining_gap_or_exclusion: No new mechanism: rechecking this exact printed graph would be a known-result formalization. Full unique-completion verification was not independently executed.

321554.title: The maximal-dimension conjecture for 1-spec matrix spaces
321554.literal_statement:
Let $V$ be a $1$-spec subspace of $\operatorname{M}_n(\mathbb{K})$ such that

$$
\dim V=1+\binom{n}{2}.
$$

Assume $n>4$. A linear subspace $W$ of $\operatorname{M}_n(\mathbb{K})$ has a **trivial spectrum** if no element of $W$ has a nonzero eigenvalue. **Maximal-dimension conjecture.** There exists a linear subspace $W$ of $\operatorname{M}_n(\mathbb{K})$ with a trivial spectrum such that

$$
V=\mathbb{K}I_n+W.
$$

The conjecture concerns the classification of $1$-spec subspaces of maximal dimension and, if true, would resolve the question for $\#\mathbb{K}>2$ and $n>4$ using the cited results on affine spaces of nonsingular matrices. Its status is not established in the supplied text.
321554.actual_review_depth: Definition 1, Conjecture 1 and adjacent trace-kernel proof in v1,v2,v3. A 2025 corrigendum was located; publisher HTTP 403.
321554.ordinary_attempt_and_prior_scope: The trace-kernel complement works when the eigenvalue is in the field and n is invertible: subtract tr(M)/n times I. This does not address absent field eigenvalues or characteristic dividing n.
321554.precise_remaining_gap_or_exclusion: Need a linear scalar-eigenvalue functional in the full 1-spec convention, including inseparable cases. The corrigendum concerns algebraic-closure spectra and n=4 and does not by itself settle n>4 here. No classification or full source clearance.

321621.title: The extension-graph conjecture for right-angled Artin groups
321621.literal_statement:
Let $\Lambda$ and $\Gamma$ be finite graphs. For a graph $\Gamma$, its **extension graph** $\Gamma^e$ has as vertices the elements of $A(\Gamma)$ conjugate to vertices of $\Gamma$, with two vertices adjacent exactly when the corresponding elements commute. Write $\Lambda\leq\Gamma^e$ when $\Lambda$ is an induced subgraph of $\Gamma^e$.

**Extension-graph conjecture.**

$$
A(\Lambda)\leq A(\Gamma)\quad\text{if and only if}\quad\Lambda\leq\Gamma^e.
$$

The forward implication is conjectured because every known embedding has arisen from an inclusion into an extension graph; the reverse implication is established by the paper's first main theorem. The conjecture remains unresolved in general, although it is proved when the target graph $\Gamma$ is triangle-free.
321621.actual_review_depth: Kim–Koberda Conjecture 4 in all three versions; Casals-Ruiz–Duncan–Kazachkov arXiv:1306.3087 Section 3, Lemma 3.1 proof and portions of Lemma 3.2.
321621.ordinary_attempt_and_prior_scope: The printed five-generator group embeds into the printed six-generator group via a -> a1 a2 and identity on b,c,d,e; Lemma 3.2 rules out induced inclusion into the extension graph. This is the exact failed implication.
321621.precise_remaining_gap_or_exclusion: Published refutation. Lemma 3.2 full case analysis and journal/version history of the counterexample paper were not completely audited; this limits review depth, not grounds to claim novelty.

321728.title: Locating chromatic number of Kneser-type Cartesian products
321728.literal_statement:
Let $n\geq 3$ and define

$$
m_0=\max\{k\mid k\in\mathbb{N},\ k(k-1)-1\leq n\}.
$$

Here $K_m$ denotes the complete graph, $\square$ the Cartesian product, and $\chi_L$ the locating chromatic number. **Locating chromatic number conjecture for $K_{m_0}\square K_n$.**

$$
\chi_L(K_{m_0}\square K_n)=n+1.
$$

The authors motivate this conjecture by verifying small cases after establishing the value in a substantial range of parameters; the remaining cases identified in the surrounding discussion are open.
321728.actual_review_depth: All three target passages; latest Lemma 2, Theorem 3 proof for complete-by-complete products and Section 4 boundary discussion.
321728.ordinary_attempt_and_prior_scope: See ORDINARY-ATTEMPTS.md: a cyclic Latin rectangle reduces to injectivity of ordered-pair colors 2a_r-a_s. At q=m(m-1) every full color must be distinct and use every available color; source greedy extension loses its last slack.
321728.precise_remaining_gap_or_exclusion: Need a uniform construction of the tight Latin rectangles, or an admissible n with a proof of nonexistence. A finite parameter check would not prove the all-n claim, and no obstructing n is supplied.

321938.title: The two-dimensional sumset lower-bound conjecture for valid multisets
321938.literal_statement:
Let $p$ be a prime and let $A$ be a **valid multiset** contained in $\mathbb{Z}_p^2$: it contains no zero element, and every nontrivial subgroup contains fewer than $p$ elements of $A$, counted with multiplicity. Write $|A|$ for the total multiplicity of $A$ and $\#\Sigma A$ for the number of distinct elements in its sumset. Assume

$$
p\leq |A|\leq 2p-3.
$$

**The two-dimensional sumset lower-bound conjecture.** Then

$$
\#\Sigma A\geq (|A|+2-p)p.
$$

Equivalently, if $|A|=p+k$ with $0\leq k\leq p-3$, then $\#\Sigma A\geq (k+2)p$. This conjecture seeks the sharp improvement of the one-dimensional lower bound for sumsets in $\mathbb{Z}_p^2$ under the validity restriction; it is the $m=2$, $q=1$ case of the wider conjecture stated later in the paper.
321938.actual_review_depth: All three source PDFs retrieved; latest Conjecture 1.6 and sharp example; journal version; Matomaki On sumsets of multisets in Z_p^m, Theorem 5 and full Section 3 proof read.
321938.ordinary_attempt_and_prior_scope: Matomaki Conjecture 4 is exactly the bound for size p+k, k<=p-3, plus an extra endpoint. Theorem 5 proves it for every k, using saturation of one-dimensional fibers, induction, and extension to size 2p-2. Therefore it directly includes the literal assigned statement.
321938.precise_remaining_gap_or_exclusion: Zero discovery credit. Auxiliary Lemmas 13–16 and publication chronology not completely independently audited; no new witness or alternative proof pursued.

322014.title: The strongly stratified and locally conical reflection arrangement conjecture
322014.literal_statement:
Let $W$ be a well-generated reflection group acting on a complex vector space $V$. A **frame** $\Lambda$ is the auxiliary structure used to define the properties strongly stratified and locally conical for the system $(W,R,\Lambda)$. **The strongly stratified and locally conical reflection arrangement conjecture.** For each well-generated reflection group $W$, there exists a generating set $R$ and a frame $\Lambda$ such that

$$
|R|=\dim V,
$$

$(W,R,\Lambda)$ is strongly stratified, and $(W,R,\Lambda)$ is locally conical. This is proposed as a partial extension of the paper's preceding results on stratification and conicality; the existence of such a generating set and frame is not established in the supplied text.
322014.actual_review_depth: Latest Definition 2.3 and Example 2.5, Definition 5.2, Conjectures 13.8–13.9; early-version geometric definitions; historical r272 result 322013.
322014.ordinary_attempt_and_prior_scope: A cone vertex must lie in every maximal face of each relevant fiber. Strong stratification additionally requires every intersection flat to carry a face of the prescribed dimension. Real Coxeter and Shephard constructions are already supplied by the source.
322014.precise_remaining_gap_or_exclusion: Need rank-sized generating reflections AND a frame for all remaining well-generated groups. A bad choice of frame does not refute the existential statement. Earlier-version target locations and journal/citing bodies not fully reviewed.

322024.title: Minimal non-face conjecture for multi-cluster complexes
322024.literal_statement:
Let $W$ be a finite Coxeter group, let $c$ be a Coxeter element, and let $\Delta_c^k(W)$ be the associated multi-cluster complex. A **minimal non-face** is an inclusion-minimal subset that is not a face.

**Minimal non-face conjecture.** Every minimal non-face of $\Delta_c^k(W)$ has cardinality $k+1$.

The lower bound $k+1$ is known in general, and the equality is established in types $A$ and $B$, for dihedral groups, and in the tested cases of ranks $3$ and $4$ with $k=2$; the general statement remains open.
322024.actual_review_depth: v3/v4 Conjecture 9.6 and following explanation, including B3 k=2 compatibility warning. v1/v2 retrieved, target passage not located by text screen.
322024.ordinary_attempt_and_prior_scope: A nonface is a set of positions meeting every reduced w0 subword of Q=c^k w0(c). Minimal nonfaces are minimal transversals; the source proves size >=k+1 and supplies A,B,dihedral cases.
322024.precise_remaining_gap_or_exclusion: Need to prove every such minimal transversal has size <=k+1 outside known types, or give a larger minimal transversal with all proper subsets verified. Pairwise incompatibility fails already in the printed B3 example; no new witness.

322081.title: The classification conjecture for APN power functions with exponent $2^t-1$
322081.literal_statement:
Let ${\mathbb F}_{2^n}$ be the finite field with $2^n$ elements, and for $2\leq t\leq n-1$ define

$$
G_t:{\mathbb F}_{2^n}\to {\mathbb F}_{2^n},\qquad G_t(x)=x^{2^t-1}.
$$

A function is **APN** if its differential uniformity is at most $2$. **The classification conjecture.** If $G_t$ is APN, then either $t=2$, or $n$ is odd and

$$
t\in\left\{\frac{n+1}{2},n-1\right\}.
$$

The three listed cases are respectively the quadratic function $x\mapsto x^3$, the function with $t=(n+1)/2$ for odd $n$, and the inverse permutation with $t=n-1$ for odd $n$. The conjecture asks whether these are the only APN functions in this family; the supplied source gives no resolution status.
322081.actual_review_depth: Both versions Conjecture 1; source conclusion and named three families. A 2022 primary problem list identifies the even-n case as solved by Gologlu.
322081.ordinary_attempt_and_prior_scope: Normalizing a nonzero derivative increment reduces APN to fibers of D_t(X)=(X+1)^(2^t-1)+X^(2^t-1). A refutation needs an additional exponent whose every derivative fiber has size <=2, not one collision-free sample.
322081.precise_remaining_gap_or_exclusion: No new exponent or uniform odd-n exclusion. Even-n result is known; Gologlu proof body and all later APN classification bodies remain unread.

322155.title: Araújo–Cohen–Giroire–Havet average-degree conjecture for critical graphs
322155.literal_statement:

322271.title: The cubic-graph cycle-length conjecture for powers of two
322271.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a cubic graph, and let $l$ be the length of a cycle in $G$. **Cubic-graph cycle-length conjecture.** There exist a cycle length $l$ in $G$ and a positive integer $k$ such that

$$
2l\leq 2^{k}<3l.
$$

The conjecture is motivated by the correspondence between cubic graphs and cubic claw-free graphs without $C_4$, together with the fact that a cycle of length $l$ in the cubic graph yields cycles of lengths from $2l$ through $3l$ in the associated claw-free graph. The source gives no resolution status, so it is recorded as open.
322271.actual_review_depth: Latest Conjecture 8 and surrounding reduction through cubic claw-free triangle expansion; earlier versions retrieved but only partial passages read.
322271.ordinary_attempt_and_prior_scope: Admissible integer cycle lengths lie in the union of intervals (2^k/3,2^(k-1)]. Triangle expansion yields lengths 2l through 3l. Selecting a shortest cycle alone does not force an admissible interval.
322271.precise_remaining_gap_or_exclusion: Need a uniform cycle-spectrum lemma for every cubic graph, or an actual cubic graph whose full cycle spectrum avoids every interval. Neither a witness nor a sound small exhaustive bound is supplied.

322351.title: Base-cobase graph diameter conjecture for block matroids
322351.literal_statement:
Let $M$ be a block matroid of rank $n$, meaning that its ground set is the disjoint union of two bases. Let $G$ be the base-cobase graph of $M$: its vertices are the bases $B$ for which the complement of $B$ in the ground set is also a base, and two vertices are adjacent when the corresponding bases differ by exactly two elements.

**Base-cobase graph diameter conjecture.** The diameter of $G$ is equal to $n$.

This is the graph-theoretic formulation, restricted to block matroids, of the serial symmetric-exchange problem. The source attributes this formulation to Cordovil and Moreira; no resolution is given there.
322351.actual_review_depth: All three Conjecture 1.4 passages; introduction and rank-four result routing.
322351.ordinary_attempt_and_prior_scope: Distance from any base to its complement is at least n because each edge replaces one element. Symmetric exchange gives neighbors, but not a path that gains one prescribed target element at every step.
322351.precise_remaining_gap_or_exclusion: Need connectivity and a sharp n-step path between arbitrary base-cobases. Restricting to graphic, transversal, sparse paving or small rank is not the exact all-matroid claim. No credible full route.

322711.literal_statement:

322716.title: Nonnegative coefficient conjecture for three-residue partition products
322716.literal_statement:
Let $L>0$, $z>1$, $y>z$, $y<x\leq y+z$, and $m\geq yz+2$. For the finite $q$-Pochhammer symbol $(a;q^m)_L=\prod_{j=0}^{L-1}(1-aq^{mj})$, define

$$
\frac{1}{(q,q^{x},q^{yz};q^{m})_L}-\frac{1}{(q^z,q^{y},q^{yz+1};q^{m})_L}=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}a(L,y,n,x,z,m)q^n.
$$

**Three-residue coefficient conjecture.** If $z$ does not divide $y$, then all coefficients $a(L,y,n,x,z,m)$ are non-negative; if $z$ divides $y$, then only finitely many of these coefficients are negative.

This conjecture extends the paper's partition inequalities to three residues and distinguishes the cases according to whether $z$ divides $y$. The authors state that it is motivated by experimental evidence and is being actively pursued; its resolution is not supplied here.
322716.actual_review_depth: All three Conjecture 5.1 passages; v1 allows 1<x<=y+z whereas v2/v3 impose y<x. Latest Theorem 4.1 proof and Theorem 4.2 comparison read. Publisher 403.
322716.ordinary_attempt_and_prior_scope: See ORDINARY-ATTEMPTS.md: product inequality gives strictly positive dominant coefficient at q=1; all other roots of unity have lower pole order, proving eventual positivity for each fixed tuple. The source already handles z=2, odd y, m=2y+2.
322716.precise_remaining_gap_or_exclusion: Missing nonnegativity of EVERY coefficient for z not dividing y. A direct residue injection lacks recoverability of original multiplicities. The eventual result is only a partial classical bridge and is not a full solution or Pi-qualified certificate.

324363.title: The Steiner subratio conjecture for the Euclidean plane
324363.literal_statement:
Let $\operatorname{ssr}(\mathbb R^2)$ denote the Steiner subratio of the Euclidean plane, defined as the infimum of the ratios of minimal-filling weight to Steiner minimal-tree length over all nontrivial finite subsets. **Steiner subratio conjecture.** The infimum is attained at the vertex set of a regular triangle and

$$
\operatorname{ssr}(\mathbb R^2)=\sqrt{3}/2.
$$

The source records the exact values for three- and four-point subsets and proposes that the global Steiner subratio has the same value, but gives no resolution of the conjecture.
324363.actual_review_depth: Latest Conjecture 5.24, surrounding three/four-point values and universal n/(2n-2) bound. Earlier 1101.0106 companion not fetched.
324363.ordinary_attempt_and_prior_scope: Regular triangle attains sqrt(3)/2; the global lower bound must compare every finite planar metric minimal filling with its Steiner minimal tree. The generic bound n/(2n-2) tends to 1/2 and cannot imply sqrt(3)/2.
324363.precise_remaining_gap_or_exclusion: No uniform geometric inequality or strict counterexample. Do not substitute the distinct classical Steiner ratio claim. Companion/version/journal coverage remains incomplete.

324369.title: Hansen's Szeged–Wiener index conjecture for bipartite graphs
324369.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a finite, simple, connected bipartite graph with $n \geq 4$ vertices and $m \geq n$ edges. Its Wiener index is

$$
W(G)=\sum_{\{u,v\}\subseteq V(G)}d(u,v),
$$

and its Szeged index is

$$
Sz(G)=\sum_{e=uv\in E(G)}n_u(e)n_v(e),
$$

where $n_u(e)$ and $n_v(e)$ count the vertices closer to $u$ and $v$, respectively, for the edge $e=uv$. **Hansen's conjecture.**

$$
Sz(G)-W(G)\geq 4n-8.
$$

The bound is best possible: equality is attained by a graph formed from a $4$-cycle $C_4$ and a tree $T$ on $n-3$ vertices sharing one vertex. The conjecture concerns a lower bound relating two classical graph indices and, in the stated source, no resolution is supplied.
324369.actual_review_depth: Source Theorem 2.2 and full proof, Lemma 2.1 full proof, Corollary 2.3 read in latest single arXiv version.
324369.ordinary_attempt_and_prior_scope: Theorem 2.2 has exactly finite simple connected bipartite n>=4,m>=n hypotheses and conclusion Sz-W>=4n-8. It decomposes into blocks after proving the two-connected case via pair contributions. Equality example also matches literally.
324369.precise_remaining_gap_or_exclusion: The source itself solves the assigned conjecture. Independent repair or formalization would not be a new outcome. Separate 1104.2122 companion and final journal body not fully read.

325182.title: The enumeration conjecture for Type B non-decreasing parking functions
325182.literal_statement:
The Type B non-decreasing parking functions are the elements of the submonoid of $\operatorname{NDPF}_{2N}$ generated by $\mu_i=\pi_i\pi_{2N-i}$ for $1\leq i\leq N$, with $\mu_N=\pi_N$. Let $C_j$ denote the $j$th Catalan number. **The BNDPF enumeration conjecture.** The cardinality of this monoid is

$$
|\operatorname{BNDPF}_N|=\sum_{j=0}^N\binom{N}{j}^2C_j.
$$

This formula agrees with all values computed through $N=9$ and with the sequence recorded as OEIS A086618, but a proof of the general enumeration was not known in the source.
325182.actual_review_depth: Single arXiv version and journal Conjecture 5.1; Section 5 definition, parabolic separation, [4321]/[4231] discussion.
325182.ordinary_attempt_and_prior_scope: Without mu_N, paired generators split into commuting halves and the source describes a double-Catalan quotient. With mu_N present, middle-boundary crossings couple the halves, so the parabolic fiber theorem cannot count the full monoid.
325182.precise_remaining_gap_or_exclusion: Need a unique normal form or explicit bijection to triples (two j-subsets of [N], a Catalan object of size j), including reachability and uniqueness. No normal form handles arbitrarily many middle-generator returns. Thesis 1108.4379 remains unread.

340762.title: Hamilton-circle conjecture from 2-connected radius-two balls
340762.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a connected, infinite, locally finite graph. A **2-connected ball of radius $2$** is the subgraph induced by the vertices in such a ball that is 2-connected. For a path $uwv$ with $uv\notin E(G)$, let $d_G(u)$ and $d_G(v)$ denote the degrees of its endpoints, and let $M_2(w)$ denote the set of vertices at distance at most $2$ from $w$.

**Hamilton-circle conjecture.** The graph $G$ has a Hamilton circle if every ball of radius $2$ in $G$ is 2-connected and

$$
d_G(u)+d_G(v)\geq |M_2(w)|-1
$$

for each path $uwv$ with $uv\notin E(G)$.

This conjecture combines local 2-connectivity with a degree condition modeled on the finite Hamiltonicity criterion. The source explicitly says that the authors believe it is true but gives no proof or resolution, so it remains open.
340762.actual_review_depth: Both versions Conjecture 2 and Fig.6 discussion; finite local-Hamiltonicity theorem routing.
340762.ordinary_attempt_and_prior_scope: Finite compatible cycles must survive an exhaustion and form a topological circle through every vertex and end. A limit of cycles can split into a disconnected spanning 2-regular object or meet an end incorrectly.
340762.precise_remaining_gap_or_exclusion: Need end-faithful connected limiting-cycle construction under the exact degree and radius-two hypotheses. A finite witness cannot by itself refute this infinite statement. Earlier three source families remain unread.

352341.title: Symmetry conjecture for optimal even small polygons
352341.literal_statement: Let $n\geq 6$ be even, and let $A_n^*$ denote the maximal area among all small $n$-gons. An **optimal $n$-gon** is a small $n$-gon whose area is $A_n^*$. Its diameter graph is the graph whose vertices are the polygon's vertices, with edges joining pairs at distance equal to the diameter, and a **pendant edge** is an edge incident to a vertex of degree one. **Symmetry conjecture.** For even $n\geq 6$, an optimal $n$-gon has an axis of symmetry corresponding to the pendant edge in its diameter graph. The maximal-area problem for even small polygons is not fully resolved; the conjecture proposes additional symmetry for optimal polygons beyond the known structure of their diameter graphs.
352341.actual_review_depth: Both versions Conjecture 1 and adjacent statements that n=6 is known; Mossinghoff family context.
352341.ordinary_attempt_and_prior_scope: Symmetric stationary polygons give lower bounds. A counterexample to the conjecture needs a globally optimal asymmetric polygon or an asymmetric feasible polygon exceeding a proved upper bound for every symmetric polygon.
352341.precise_remaining_gap_or_exclusion: No global extremal certificate. Source diameter-graph theorem does not force axial symmetry. Earlier 1103.4456 and all optimizer proof bodies not read.
